content: 1. Minimal changes in drug concentrations can result in severe or life-threatening toxicities. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates should be avoided or alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate as per product labeling. 2. Voxilaprevir increases the levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant through mechanisms other than CYP enzymes. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Velpatasvir also increases the levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant through similar mechanisms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. OATP1B3 inhibitors can significantly increase the systemic exposure of zavegepant, which is an OATP1B3 substrate. Acalabrutinib increases velpatasvir levels through inhibition of intestinal BCRP transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Acalabrutinib may increase exposure to coadministered BCRP substrates. 4. Apalutamide decreases velpatasvir levels by increasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. Apalutamide weakly induces BCRP and may reduce systemic exposure of drugs that are BCRP substrates. 5. Atazanavir increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Voxilaprevir increases atogepant levels through mechanisms other than CYP enzymes. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Velpatasvir also increases atogepant levels through similar mechanisms. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dosage with OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg daily. 6. Berotralstat increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Berotralstat also increases voxilaprevir levels through P-gp inhibition. Voxilaprevir increases berotralstat levels through other mechanisms. Monitor for adverse effects when berotralstat, a BCRP substrate, is coadministered with a BCRP inhibitor. 7. Cannabidiol increases velpatasvir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cannabidiol may inhibit CYP2C8 activity. Cannabidiol also increases voxilaprevir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Cannabidiol may induce or inhibit CYP2B6, necessitating dosage adjustments of CYP2B6 substrates. 8. Cenobamate decreases velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP2B6 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 9. Danicopan increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Danicopan also increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, necessitating dose reductions of sensitive P-gp substrates to avoid serious adverse reactions. 10. Chloramphenicol increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin, cobicistat, and conivaptan similarly increase velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 11. Fostamatinib increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-gp and BCRP transporters. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp/BCRP substrate drugs and consider dosage reductions when coadministered with fostamatinib. 12. Fostemsavir increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates when coadministered with fostemsavir. 13. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases voxilaprevir and velpatasvir levels by inhibiting P-gp and BCRP transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor plasma concentrations of P-gp and BCRP substrates. 14. Idelalisib increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir similarly increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 15. Istradefylline increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of P-gp and CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed with 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 16. Itraconazole increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Lemborexant decreases velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor CYP2B6 substrates for adequate clinical response and consider increasing their dose as per prescribing recommendations. 18. Lenacapavir increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 19. Voxilaprevir increases letermovir levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 20. Lonafarnib increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor. Monitor for adverse reactions when coadministered with P-gp substrates, and reduce the dose of P-gp substrates if needed. 21. Mavorixafor increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Velpatasvir increases mavorixafor levels by inhibiting P-gp transporters. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 22. Mifepristone increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Voxilaprevir increases momelotinib toxicity through mechanisms such as plasma protein binding competition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Momelotinib increases velpatasvir toxicity through similar mechanisms. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase exposure to BCRP substrates, necessitating dose adjustments. 24. Nefazodone increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Nelfinavir similarly increases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 25. Nirmatrelvir increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir also increases voxilaprevir levels through similar mechanisms. 26. Omaveloxolone decreases velpatasvir and voxilaprevir levels by reducing systemic exposure of sensitive CYP2C8 substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. Check prescribing information for dosage modifications of CYP2C8 substrates.
